text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mixed in quiet dealings. Business was routine with a late uptick largely reflecting end-week position squaring. August closed at $324.30 per tonne, up $0.60, while October closed at $316.60 per tonne, down $1.20.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed mostly lower after setting new contract highs earlier on, as continued pressure on the nearby switch dragged the overall market lower. July lost 7 points to close at 11.42 cents/lb. October gave up 2 points to close at 11.32 cents/lb which pulled the July/October switch down to 10 points from 15 points on Thursday. With July's options expiry now out of the way, traders said the focus will turn to the July futures contract, which goes off the board at the end of the month.

INDIA - India produced 1.54 million tonnes of sugar, white value, in April, compared with 2.13 million tonnes the same month in 1996, the Indian Sugar Mills Association and the National Confederation of Cooperative Sugar Factories Ltd said in a joint statement. This brought total production since the beginning of 1996/97 up to 12.3 million tonnes, down from 13.9 million tonnes produced the same period in 1995/96.

Production up to the end of April points to a seasonally adjusted total of 13.6 million tonnes, which compares to the latest estimate of the Indian Sugar Mills Association of 13 million tonnes. Production in 1995/96 was 16.5 million tonnes. Sugar dispatches from factories in April stood at 1.1 million tonnes for domestic consumption and 15,000 tonnes for exports which compares to 940,000 and 109,000 tonnes respectively the same month last year. Sugar stocks on April 30 stood at 11.8 million tonnes compared with 11.4 million tonnes on the same date in 1996, the statement said.

MOZAMBIQUE - Sugar production in Mozambique in 1997/98 (May/April) is forecast to reach 48,500 tonnes, tel quel, up from 29,288 tonnes produced in 1996/97 and 28,351 tonnes produced in 1995/96. Sugar consumption in 1996/97 is expected to reach 67,700 tonnes, up from 53,880 tonnes the previous year.

Philippine President Fidel Ramos has authorized the import of about 27,000 tonnes of sugar from the world market to replace its planned export of the same volume to the United States. The state agency National Food Authority (NFA) or its assigned agent will be given tariff-free privileges to make the imports.
